Ran both Makefile check targets and a one-iteration benchmark-driver smoke check
Ran 21 independent edge assertions covering invocation, status, redirection mode, built-in context, process groups, jobs, and fg

Reviewed source, tests, learner documentation, progressive-disclosure boundaries, provenance/license statements, and validation-label claims

All 21 independent edge assertions passed, including equal pipeline PGIDs and announced PGID, umask-filtered mode 0640, monotonic job IDs, and default fg selection
The timeout harness removed a SIGTERM-ignoring descendant through bounded SIGKILL escalation in 0.704 seconds
The packaging audit reported 23 required files, 0 forbidden paths, 57 audited entries, 42 scanned regular files, strict metadata consistency, and a verified provenance-document digest

The provenance document SHA-256 was 8aa702b8b64241bda70f3a63e3d1b9a681e7dc87f4d5930b9b4f764f584e5dad; the 42-file aggregate was unchanged at b6e6cb39b1c6905f1d192fdbafdecd41a67eb34e531de14040cd9d79172b2099
MANIFEST.yaml remains GENERATED/PARTIAL with independent validation REQUIRED and productionized false; builder prose explicitly disclaims promoted validation labels
Learner-facing requirements, concepts, questions, starter, and public tests are separated from clearly marked sealed and harness-only material; the reference documents its non-production gaps
limitations: The immutable upstream catalog object database and linked tutorial were unavailable and network access was not used, so source hashes, upstream license evidence, and the no-copy assertion were not independently recomputed
No orchestrator-created learner view was available, so actual transfer-time exclusion of sealed and harness-only material was not verified

Validation covered one Linux/POSIX host with Python 3.11.5 and GCC 15.2.0; it did not cover the stated Python 3.9 minimum, other POSIX systems, fault injection, coverage-guided fuzzing, or production readiness
LeakSanitizer was not exercised, and the benchmark was only a driver smoke check with no acceptance threshold
environment/check.sh validates fewer runtime fixtures than the supplied suites use, so its prerequisites-present message is not a complete portability preflight
The first isolated-copy build attempt was inconclusive because cp -a preserved the submission's read-only modes; changing only scratch-copy modes produced the successful results reported above
